title: Place and direction questions review
focus: Ask where, where from and where to, and build answers with bounded common location forms.
targetSkills: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms

exercises.prompt: Write “Where is the pen?” in Finnish. Use kynä (“pen”), on (“is”).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The inessive is the in-place form, answering where. Missä asks where someone or something is. For the inside-location pattern, put -ssa or -ssä on the taught noun stem. There is no movement into or out of the place. The complete question means “Where is the pen”.

parts.role: question asking where someone or something is

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)

exercises.prompt: Write “Where are they going?” in Finnish. Use he (“they”), menevät (“go”).
